summary.intent: Split the overloaded `delta` skill (and other multi-verb plugin skills) into targeted skills, add a consumer-focused changeset/semver model with a shared docs-voice standard, and harden the repo with validation scripts and CI.
summary.outcome: Split delta into six skills and canon/graph/basis similarly, added changeset@2/release-artifact@2 schemas, docs-voice.md, topic-based changeset apportionment, three check scripts with shared lib, and a CI workflow. Pushed to main and tagged delta--v2.1.1.

repo: Before this session every plugin had exactly one skill directory, with a thin dispatcher fanning out to subagents; delta, canon, graph and basis were later split into multiple skills, and the constitution was amended to allow it.
shared/constitution.md makes schemas immutable: a breaking change requires a new @N+1 file (changeset@2, release-artifact@2) and all consumers must be repointed.
Skill naming: default is a single word, but a specific multi-word name (e.g. post-review) is preferred over a <plugin>-<stage> prefix, since plugin:skill invocation already disambiguates.

Two marketplace manifests are both sources of truth and are synced manually: root marketplace.json (id/path/version per plugin) and .claude-plugin/marketplace.json (Claude Code schema, no per-plugin version).
changesets.md has a skip list (pure docs, reference updates, internal refactors) that must be checked before the semver table; tooling-only changes need no bump.

Changeset apportionment priority: shared linked_spec/plan/requirement, then explicitly stated shared scope, then shared cause inferred from the diff; it is not a proxy for file/package/commit count, and both over-bundling and over-splitting are failure modes.
Unquoted @ in Mermaid labels breaks rendering under the newer grammar and must be quoted; verify by rendering with @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli, not by reading source.
Standing rule: never hard-wrap markdown, changesets, commit messages, or PR bodies.
macOS BSD grep lacks -P; use -E in scripts.
claude plugin tag plugins/<name> --push creates <plugin>--v<version> tags validated against the marketplace entry.

code.finding: Shared report_check() holds the OK/FAILED summary used by check-mermaid.sh, check-versions.sh and check-skills-doc.sh; each script passes its own wording and the exit 1 propagates under set -e.
Matches only table rows of the form | `plugin/skill` | because free prose in READMEs legitimately negates fictional skills (e.g. 'no `proof/scan`'), which caused false positives.
Compares four sources by string equality: plugin.json version, README **Version:** line, top CHANGELOG ## [X.Y.Z] entry, and root marketplace.json per-plugin version.

workflow: Verify against authoritative sources (gh api, WebFetch, actually running tools) instead of reconstructing from memory; memory-based CODE_OF_CONDUCT and Mermaid assumptions produced real errors.
Test new checks by injecting deliberate drift and confirming they fail, so they don't pass vacuously.
Plan mode before large restructures, as the user asked, helped catch the constitution violations on audit.
Use shellcheck from the scripts directory so source directives resolve; invoking from the repo root with -x produced a spurious failure.
Verify a git staging area before committing: pre-staged git rm deletions leaked into an unrelated release commit and had to be fixed with reset --soft.
Research subagents (style guides, prior art) kept the main context focused on synthesis.

friction: Initially edited changeset@1/release-artifact@1 in place, violating schema immutability; reverted and created @2 files.
Named a skill post-review then renamed it post and reverted back after user pushback, costing churn across several files.
Early SKILL.md files were hard-wrapped before the user's no-wrap rule and needed rework.
First release commit accidentally included unrelated staged deletions.
Tagged v3.0.0 with no earlier history and bumped for pure doc changes (v3.1.0); needed backfilled tags and a process fix.
check-versions.sh failed first on BSD grep -P; check-skills-doc.sh false-positived on negation prose.
Several mid-session reconstructions from memory (CODE_OF_CONDUCT, Mermaid) were wrong and had to be redone.
The callisto fork committed to the wrong branch and was fixed by cherry-picking onto main.
open_items: Plan Phase 4 (dogfood delta/changeset against this repo's own diff) was never run.
Markdown tooling deferred: markdownlint-cli2 vs Prettier vs Vale (Vale could enforce docs-voice.md banned words, but it is a Go binary breaking the npx precedent).
Pre-existing unused-field warnings in plugin.json surfaced by claude plugin tag --dry-run were not addressed.

The skills/<id>/SKILL.md directory layout was amended in the constitution, but whether other plugins (proof, vector, lambda, trace, axiom) should split was judged unnecessary because they are linear pipelines.
Possible future naming collision: canon's 'changeset' concept (spec corrections) versus delta's changeset skill if canon splits further.
